name: Alleppey
tagline: The Venice of the East amid Kerala's backwaters.
whenBlurb: November to March is the dry, green backwater season for houseboats; the June-September monsoon suits Ayurveda, and August's Onam brings the great snake-boat races.

ourTake.lede: Alleppey is the gateway to the Kerala backwaters, and the mistake is treating it as a town, the point is to get onto the water. Take a private houseboat overnight rather than the crowded day cruises, and choose the smaller canals over the wide main lake. Time it for the evening, when the boats moor and the paddy fields go quiet. Late-August boat-race season is spectacular but busy.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a private houseboat on the backwaters and unhurried Kerala calm.
ourTake.skipIf: You want sightseeing, nightlife or a fast-moving itinerary.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Spice Routes Luxury Cruises (private houseboat charter)
credentials: Pioneer of ultra-luxury Alleppey houseboats since 2008, 5-star hospitality afloat
1- to 5-bedroom private boats, each with driver, assistant and personal cook
AC cabins with ensuite bathrooms; the whole boat is chartered to your party alone
items.description: The iconic Kerala experience at its most private, your own air-conditioned kettuvallam with a dedicated crew and personal cook, drifting the backwaters as they should be seen.

items.name: Purity at Lake Vembanad
credentials: Malabar Escapes, the sister hotel to The Malabar House, Fort Kochi (that group's first Relais & Châteaux member)
MICHELIN Guide hotels-stays selection, Purity at Lake Vembanad (hotel selection)
Heritage-, art- and luxury-hotel in one; own houseboat, Ayurvedic spa, yoga and cruises
items.description: Malabar Escapes' lakefront jewel, an art-filled villa hotel where every terrace opens onto Vembanad at its widest, reached by a short boat across the water.

items.name: Marari Beach Resort, a CGH Earth Experience
credentials: CGH Earth flagship beach resort, garden villas, pool villas and deluxe villas with private pools
Marari Beach rated among the world's top-5 'Hammock Beaches' by National Geographic
Chakara coastal-Kerala restaurant, Beach Grill and an organic farm-to-table kitchen; renowned Ayurveda centre
items.description: CGH Earth's barefoot-luxury beach village, thatched Kerala villas across coconut groves and lily ponds, many with a private pool, on one of India's quietest beaches.

items.name: Xandari Pearl Beach Resort
credentials: Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice, Best of the Best (Small Hotels), 2021
27 villas over 18 acres, 12 with private plunge pools; each with a large private garden and sandy sit-out
Farm-to-table dining, Ayura Spa, beach yoga and cooking demonstrations
items.description: Twenty-seven private villas across 18 acres of the Marari fishing village, sky-open showers, plunge pools and a farm-to-table kitchen, moments from the sand.

items.name: Kayaloram Heritage Lake Resort
credentials: Classified a heritage property by the Government of India
Traditional carved-timber tile-roofed cottages, lake-facing, around a pool and butterfly garden
On-site Ayurveda centre and its own refurbished rice-barge houseboat for backwater cruises
items.description: A Government-classified heritage resort of carved-wood Kerala cottages on Vembanad Lake, a butterfly garden, an infinity edge and an Ayurveda centre a short hop from Alappuzha.

items.name: Punnamada Resort
credentials: Lakefront villas in traditional Kerala style, slanted roofs, heavy carved-wood doors and windows
Overlooks Punnamada Lake and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race finishing waters
Pool, multi-cuisine restaurant and its own houseboats for backwater cruising
items.description: Kerala-architecture villas on the banks of Punnamada, the very stretch of water where the Nehru Trophy snake boats race each August.

items.name: Lake Palace Resort
credentials: Backwater lake resort on the banks of Punnamada and Vembanad Lake
Traditional Kerala-style cottages set in gardens by the water
Ayurvedic wellness and houseboat cruises arranged from the resort jetty
items.description: A backwater lake resort on the Punnamada shore, traditional cottages, an Ayurveda centre and the lake framing every view.

items.name: The overnight kettuvallam houseboat cruise
items.description: The signature of the whole region: a converted rice barge, all curved wood and palm-thatch, that becomes your private floating hotel for a night. A crew of three cooks your dinner on board, ties up beside a village at dusk, and casts off again at first light through mist rising off the water. The honeymoon and multi-generation classic, best taken as a single crewed boat for your family alone.

items.name: A private crewed houseboat, chef aboard
items.description: Beyond the standard boat, the top operators run one- and two-bedroom kettuvallams with a dedicated cook, upper sun-deck and glass-walled bedrooms, taken exclusively for your party. The kitchen runs to the fresh catch of the day and a full vegetarian Kerala spread, and the itinerary bends to you rather than the fleet. This is how UHNI families do the backwaters.

items.name: Vembanad Lake at its widest
credentials: Part of the Vembanad-Kol wetland, a Ramsar site of international importance
items.description: The largest lake in Kerala and the longest in India, opening from the green canals into a horizon of flat silver water. This is the great backwater expanse the houseboats drift across in the afternoon, dotted with Chinese fishing nets and the low green line of Kumarakom on the far shore.

items.name: A sunset on Vembanad Lake
items.description: The single most photographed hour in Kerala: the sun dropping into the flat lake water, the sky turning copper and rose, silhouetted fishermen hauling nets, and the boat gone quiet. Taken from the deck of your own houseboat or a small shikara pushed out onto the open water, it is the region's quiet emotional peak.

items.name: The shikara village-canal tour
items.description: The narrow inner canals the big houseboats can never reach, threaded by a low, quiet shikara or dugout canoe. Palms lean overhead until they nearly touch, and you pass within feet of front doorsteps, women beating coir, and children waving from the banks. This is the postcard Kerala that only a small boat can show you.

items.name: A dawn canoe through the paddy country
items.description: Before the heat, a poled country canoe slips out along the mirror-still canals between the paddy bunds, past herons and the first fishermen. Slower and quieter even than the shikara, it is the most intimate way onto the water, and the light at that hour is unmatched.

items.name: Alleppey Beach and the old pier
items.description: Where the backwaters meet the Arabian Sea, with a weathered iron pier stretching out over the surf, a colonial-era lighthouse and the Vijaya Beach Park behind it. The pier is over a century old and makes for a fine evening stroll after the slow days on the water.

items.name: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
items.description: Across Vembanad Lake on the old Baker rubber estate, a compact sanctuary of over 180 species: egrets, herons, darters, kingfishers, and in winter the migratory flocks. Best walked in the early morning or seen from a boat gliding along the fringe. A serene, cultured half-day for the naturalist in the family.

items.name: The Kumarakom backwaters, across the lake
items.description: The quieter, more resort-lined shore of Vembanad, reached across the water from Alleppey. Kumarakom trades the town's houseboat traffic for hushed lakeside lawns and slower canals, and it is where several of the region's finest properties sit right on the water's edge.

items.name: Pathiramanal Island
items.description: A small, uninhabited island marooned in the middle of Vembanad Lake, its name meaning 'sands of midnight'. Reached only by boat, it is a birder's secret with some ninety species, butterflies and dense greenery, and makes a lovely, little-visited pause on a lake crossing.

items.name: Marari Beach and the fishing village
items.description: A long, quiet ribbon of sand backed by coconut groves and a working fishing hamlet, half an hour from Alleppey. The daily fish auction on the shore is a piece of unhurried coastal life, and the beach itself is where the backwaters trip earns its seaside days.

items.name: Marari Beach Resort, a CGH Earth property
items.description: The reimagined fishing village on twelve hectares of coconut grove and lily pond, with clay-tiled cottages, private-pool villas, an organic farm and an Ayurveda centre using herbs grown on site. The barefoot-luxury counterpoint to a houseboat night, and a favourite for families who want the beach with the backwaters.

items.name: The Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race
items.description: The vallam kali: hundred-foot chundan snake boats, over a hundred oarsmen each, driven down Punnamada Lake to the beat of the vanchipattu boat song. Held every August since Nehru inaugurated it in 1952, it is Kerala's greatest spectacle, and the finish-line pavilion tickets are the way to see it in comfort.

items.name: The Champakulam Moolam Boat Race
items.description: The oldest snake-boat race in the region, run on the Pamba River past the ancient St Mary's church, and far less thronged than the Nehru Trophy. Seen from a riverbank close enough to feel the spray, it is the intimate, traditional face of vallam kali.

items.name: Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna Temple
items.description: A fifteenth-century temple to Krishna in the rare Parthasarathi form, and home to the palpayasam, a milk-rice pudding so famous that legend says the god himself comes daily to taste it. A short drive from town, it is the region's most beloved temple and the sweet offering is worth the queue.

items.name: Mullakkal Rajarajeswari Temple
items.description: The living heart of Alleppey town, a five-centuries-old temple to the goddess Rajarajeswari on the bustling Mullakkal shopping street. Its festivals fill the streets, and it is the easiest way to feel the town's own devotional pulse between backwater days.

items.name: St Mary's Forane Church, Champakulam
items.description: One of the oldest Christian churches in Kerala, tradition dating it to the fourth century, standing on the Pamba riverbank at the heart of the Syrian Christian backwater country. A cool, ornate interior and a deep history that predates almost everything else on the water.

items.name: Chennamkary and Champakulam village life
items.description: The rice-paddy villages laced with canals where the real Kuttanad lives: fishermen, coir-spinners, duck herders and toddy-tappers going about their day. Explored on foot and by canoe, it is the human landscape behind the scenery, and the reason a shikara trip here feels like a visit rather than a view.

items.name: The Kuttanad paddy fields below sea level
credentials: Recognised by the FAO as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS)
items.description: One of the few places on earth, with the Netherlands, where farming happens up to two metres below the sea, the paddy reclaimed from the lake behind dikes and kept dry by constant pumping. Green squares of rice ringed by water, it is a quietly astonishing feat of human ingenuity.

items.name: The R-Block kayal lands
items.description: The most dramatic of the reclaimed fields, vast rectangles of paddy walled off from the open lake itself, where you can stand on a bund with water on both sides above the level of the crop. The engineering heart of below-sea-level farming, and a striking detour few visitors reach.

items.name: A coir-making village walk
items.description: Alleppey was built on coir, and along the inner canals the fibre is still extracted from coconut husk, beaten, sorted and spun by hand, much as it was a century ago. A guided walk through these hamlets is a warm, tactile look at the craft that made the town.

items.name: A toddy shop (kallu shaap) lunch
items.description: The most authentic Kerala meal you can eat: a rustic riverside shack serving fiery karimeen fry, kappa and meen curry, and the fresh, faintly sweet fermented palm sap called kallu. Earthy, generous and far better than any tourist restaurant, it is a cultural rite as much as a meal, arranged privately for those who prefer.

items.name: Karumadikuttan, the black granite Buddha
items.description: A weathered, half-broken Buddha of black granite dating perhaps to the ninth century, lost for centuries in a stream until a colonial engineer recovered it. A quiet reminder of the Buddhist past of this coast, and a moving, uncrowded stop near Ambalappuzha.

items.name: Revi Karunakaran Memorial Museum
items.description: A private museum built by a coir baron's widow, holding one of the world's largest private collections of Swarovski crystal alongside carved ivory, jade, porcelain and Tanjore paintings. An unexpectedly opulent hour in the middle of town.

items.name: Krishnapuram Palace and the Gajendra Moksha mural
credentials: Holds India's largest mural painting, the Gajendra Moksham
items.description: An eighteenth-century Travancore palace near Kayamkulam that holds India's largest single mural: the forty-nine-square-metre Gajendra Moksham, the salvation of the elephant king. The Kettukazhcha architecture and the mural together make it the region's finest heritage stop.

items.name: The Thanneermukkom bund
items.description: The great barrier thrown across Vembanad Lake in the 1970s, the largest mud regulator in India, built to keep the sea's salt out of the Kuttanad rice country. Standing on it, with the lake stretching away on both sides, is the clearest way to grasp how this whole watery landscape is engineered.

items.name: The eight-hour Alleppey-to-Kollam backwater cruise
items.description: The longest single stretch of open backwater in Kerala, running south from Alleppey through Kumarakom and on to the Ashtamudi lake at Kollam. A full day across lakes, lagoons, rivers and canals, it is the grand traverse for those who want the water without stopping.

items.name: Ashtamudi Lake at Kollam
items.description: The eight-armed lake at the southern end of the backwaters, quieter and less touristed than Vembanad, fringed with coconut groves and old cashew warehouses. A day-trip or the far anchor of the long cruise, and a lovely place to see the backwaters at their most serene.

items.name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
items.description: The 'Kashi of the South', an ancient Shiva temple on the Vembanad shore with classic Kerala architecture, and the site of the 1924 Vaikom Satyagraha that Gandhi joined against untouchability. History and devotion in one, reached easily across the lake.

items.name: A backwater-resort Ayurveda spa
items.description: Kerala is the home of Ayurveda, and the lakeside resorts run serious wellness centres, from a single restorative abhyanga massage to a multi-day panchakarma programme, oils pressed from herbs grown on the property. The slow, restorative counterweight to the water days.

items.name: Purity at Lake Vembanad
credentials: Relais & Chateaux member property
items.description: A fourteen-room Relais & Chateaux villa on the western shore of the lake, all minimalist elegance, gourmet cuisine, a private houseboat and an Ayurvedic spa. The most design-forward small retreat on the backwaters, and a favourite of the discerning couple.

items.name: Kumarakom Lake Resort
items.description: Twenty-five acres of heritage villas, a meandering pool, the Ayurmana spa and its own stretch of Vembanad shore, a repeat World Travel Award winner for India's leading resort. The grand-luxury address on the water for a multi-generation stay.

items.name: Kayaloram Lake Resort
items.description: An intimate cluster of tiled Kerala cottages set right on the Vembanad shore near Alleppey, reached by the resort's own boat, with lawns running down to the water. A quieter, more traditional lakeside base for those who want the backwaters without a crowd.

items.name: A private lake cruise at golden hour
items.description: Not the overnight boat but a short, chartered evening cruise on a shikara or the resort's own launch, out onto the open lake for the sunset and back for dinner. The perfect low-commitment way to have the water and the light without a full houseboat night.

items.name: Watch a Kathakali performance
items.description: Kerala's temple dance-drama, all towering headdress, painted green faces and slow, precise storytelling, staged in the evening at the cultural centres and the larger resorts. A concentrated dose of the state's classical arts between backwater days.

items.name: A cooking session with a Kerala home cook
items.description: In a village home or aboard a private houseboat, learning the coconut, curry-leaf and tamarind grammar of Kerala cooking: the karimeen, the avial, the vegetarian sadya. A hands-on way to carry the region's flavours home, and easily arranged for a family.

items.name: Explore Alleppey's canal town on foot
items.description: The 'Venice of the East' still runs on its old canals and coir warehouses, its 1862 grid of waterways crossed by little bridges and lined with faded trading houses. A morning walk past the Mullakkal market and the old harbour gives the town its context before you take to the water.

items.name: See the Chinese fishing nets at work
items.description: The great cantilevered shore-operated nets, dipped and hauled by teams of fishermen along the canals and lakeshore, are one of the enduring images of the Kerala coast. Watch a haul come up, or buy the catch straight off the net for your boat's kitchen.

items.name: A duck-village and paddy morning
items.description: Kuttanad's herders drive great rafts of ducks along the canals between the flooded fields, and a slow morning by canoe among them, past farmers on the bunds and the birds rising off the water, is village life at its most unspoiled.

items.name: Sunrise from your anchored houseboat
items.description: The overlooked half of the overnight cruise: waking on the still water at dawn, mist lifting off the canal, the village stirring, and a cup of Kerala coffee on the deck before the boat moves. The quietest and most private moment the backwaters give you.

items.name: The R-Block and Rani-Chithira kayal drive
items.description: For those who want the below-sea-level country up close and dry, a drive along the bund roads through the great reclaimed kayal blocks, water lapping above the fields on either side. A rarely-taken route that lets you photograph the phenomenon from land.

items.name: A visit to a working coir factory
items.description: Beyond the village spinning, Alleppey's old coir factories still weave the mats and matting that made the town's name, on hand and power looms in cavernous colonial sheds. A short, characterful stop that closes the loop on what a kettuvallam is knotted from.

items.name: Punnamada Lake and the snake-boat sheds
items.description: Even out of race season, the finishing lake of the Nehru Trophy is worth the short trip, and in the villages nearby the hundred-foot chundan boats rest in their long thatched sheds, tended like heirlooms. A chance to stand beside one of these giants is a quiet thrill.

items.name: Chakara, Marari Beach Resort
credentials: Signature restaurant at Marari Beach Resort (CGH Earth)
Farm-to-table from the resort's organic garden; Chemeen Manga Curry, Kozhi Kurumulagu roast and the day's fish
Beach Grill and cooking demonstrations alongside
items.description: CGH Earth's coastal-Kerala kitchen, the day's catch and produce handpicked from the resort's own four-acre organic farm.

items.name: Dining at Purity, Lake Vembanad
credentials: The kitchen of Purity at Lake Vembanad (Malabar Escapes; Michelin Guide hotel selection)
Gourmet, produce-led menus in the group's Malabar House lineage
Lakefront dining, and dishes served aboard the hotel's own houseboat
items.description: Malabar Escapes' lakefront table, gourmet cooking of Keralan produce, served on a terrace over Vembanad at its widest.

items.name: The chef's table aboard a private houseboat
credentials: Every premium Alleppey houseboat carries a personal onboard cook (Spice Routes, CGH Earth's Spice Coast Cruises)
Fresh karimeen (pearl-spot), freshwater prawns and Kuttanad specialities cooked to order
Served on your private deck as the boat moors for the night
items.description: Not a restaurant but the region's signature meal, your kettuvallam's own cook grilling the karimeen and prawns bought that morning from the water.

items.name: Thaff
credentials: A long-standing, well-regarded Alappuzha restaurant
Known for karimeen pollichathu, Kuttanadan duck roast, crispy prawns and Kerala meals
items.description: The town's go-to for Kerala home cooking and Indo-Chinese, karimeen pollichathu and Kuttanadan duck roast among the orders.

items.name: Halais Restaurant
credentials: A popular, family-friendly Alappuzha institution
Biryanis, kebabs, Arabic grills and traditional Kerala thali meals
items.description: A clean, family-run Alappuzha standby for biryanis, kebabs and Kerala meals, Arabic and Indian side by side.

items.name: Resort bars, Marari Beach & Purity
credentials: Bar and beach-grill service at Marari Beach Resort (CGH Earth)
Lakefront bar and terrace at Purity (Malabar Escapes)
items.description: For a proper drink, the resort bars, a beachside sundowner at Marari or a lakefront one at Purity, in safe, well-kept hands.

items.name: Sundowners aboard your houseboat
credentials: A private chef-crewed houseboat moored for the evening (Spice Routes; CGH Earth's Spice Coast Cruises)
The definitive Alleppey evening, sunset over Vembanad, then stillness and stars
items.description: The only 'night out' that matters here, a drink on your own moored deck as the light goes over the paddy and the water falls silent.

plan.heading: 2 days in Alleppey, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Board a private, well-crewed houseboat at Punnamada, or settle into a lakeside villa at Purity on Vembanad, and drift out through the narrow canals.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A slow afternoon along the Kuttanad paddy waterways below sea level, stopping at a toddy-tapper's village and a coir workshop.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A karimeen and prawn dinner cooked aboard by your chef as the boat moors for the night among the palms.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early canoe through the fine channels the houseboat can't reach, watching the village wake and the fishermen at their nets.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Cross Vembanad Lake to Purity or the Marari coast for lunch and time by the water, then a Kalari or Ayurveda session.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quiet last dinner of Kerala coastal cooking on the lakefront, with the fishing lamps out on the water.

items.name: Punnamada / backwater edge
items.description: Where the houseboats launch and the race is held, on the water, not in town.

items.name: Marari Beach
items.description: A quiet fishing coast just north, for beach and calm alongside the backwaters.

items.name: Kumarakom (Vembanad)
items.description: Across the lake with the bird sanctuary and top resorts, for lakeside seclusion.

events.name: Nehru Trophy Boat Race
events.note: Kerala's most famous snake-boat race on Punnamada Lake, the 2026 edition is 22 August.

events.name: Onam
events.note: Kerala's harvest festival, with flower carpets, feasts and village boat races; date follows the Malayalam calendar.

events.name: Champakulam Moolam Boat Race
events.note: Kerala's oldest snake-boat race, on the Pamba river near Alleppey.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Charter a private houseboat rather than a shared cruiser, and ask for one moored in the quieter canals overnight away from the main channel; October to March is the settled season, and the mosquitoes reward good repellent at dusk.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Cochin International Airport (COK), about a 90-minute chauffeured drive south to Alleppey; from there, board your houseboat or resort jetty directly.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private houseboat or solar-electric backwater cruiser for the lagoons and canals, and a private car with driver for the road to Kumarakom and the coast.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Jio and Airtel 4G is reliable near town but thins out on the deeper backwaters; treat time on the water as genuinely offline.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; carry cash for village stops, toddy shops and small purchases, as cards are limited once you are on the water; tip the boat crew at journey's end.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November to February is ideal for the backwaters, dry and 17-32C; avoid mid-July to September, when heavy monsoon makes houseboat cruising unpleasant, and the hot March-May off-season.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No airport; fly to Cochin International (COK), then about a 1.5-hour drive south (about 83 km). COK takes direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru; travel the long leg in business on a Gulf carrier or from your metro origin, then transfer straight to the houseboat jetty.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations beyond routine Hepatitis A/Typhoid; carry mosquito repellent for the waterways, especially at dusk. Safe and slow-paced. Drink only sealed or filtered water; backwater water is not potable.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Very easy: the classic Kerala sadya served on the houseboats is vegetarian by default, and crews will cook to preference. Jain is understood if arranged in advance. Ask for the estate-style veg sadya on premium houseboats such as Spice Coast Cruises.
